question.leadin: Answer these questions about Spanish conquistadores.
question.text: This figure defeated a much larger force than his own at the battle of Cajamarca before conquering the Inca empire in 1532.
question.clue: He accompanied Vasco de Balboa in his voyage to Panama and launched a successful ambush at the Battle of Cajamarca; that attack took place shortly after the death of Huascar.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about colonial explorers who met violent ends.
swap.text: The conquistador Francisco Pizarro, who conquered this empire, was killed in a violent attack orchestrated by Diego de Almagro II. Pizarro himself had this Andean empire's ruler Atahualpa executed in 1533.
swap.clue: This empire's capital city, Cuzco, was captured by the conquistador Francisco Pizarro.

question.text: Timur allegedly built pyramids out of these body parts, the protective structure for the brain, which would terrify his enemies.
question.clue: After sacking Ankara in Turkey, Tamerlane allegedly made a pyramid of these objects.

swap.leadin: Like the related Aymaras, the women of this ethnic group often wear bowler hats.
swap.text: Identify this ethnic group that is indigenous to the Andes. The language of this ethnic group was used by the Incans to record messages on quipus.
swap.answerHtml: Quechua [accept more specific groups such as Runakuna, Kichwas, or Ingas]
swap.clue: The MUPP-NP party's common name is a word in this language that's gained popularity with indigenists for its connotation of "world reversal."

question.leadin: Women new to this city were sent to schools called acllahuasi ("ock-yah-WAH-see"), where they were trained to become secluded virgins who brewed chicha.
question.text: Name this former capital that was shaped like a jaguar and built from stone without using mortar. This capital surrendered after Atalhualpa was captured at Cajamarca.
question.clue: A chief of this puma-shaped city adopted a name roughly translated as "world turner."

swap.leadin: Name some things about the downfall of the Incan Empire.
swap.text: The downfall of the Incan empire began when Pizarro launched this surprise attack on the royal Incan family. Pizarro's capture of the Inca here led to him demanding a room full of gold as ransom.
swap.clue: The losing side in this battle was engaged in a civil war against Huascar and was crippled by the decision to leave the bulk of its army outside the city walls.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Andean civilizations.
question.text: This culture existed in the Ica river valley succeeding the Paracas culture. These people are famous for theirnamesake lines which form geoglyphs visible from the sky.

swap.text: The mita was used by Spanish rulers to obtain a labor force for this largest silver mine in the Spanish Empire, in which thousands died from mercury poisoning. It lies in present-day Bolivia.
swap.clue: Economic production in this city took off following the remote discovery of Huancavelica, which supplied material crucial for a process invented by Bartolome de Medina widely used in this city.

question.leadin: The execution of Antonio de Arriaga instigated a rebellion led by a man with this regnal name.
question.text: Give this two-word name of an indigenous Peruvian rebel leader who claimed descent from the final Sapa Inca. That Neo-Incan ruler with this regnal name was executed by the Spanish in 1572.
question.clue: The legitimate son of Manco Capac, he was captured an executed for the death of Friar Diego Ortiz.

swap.leadin: A first-year undergrad named Manny Medrano helped decode a system used in these things.
swap.text: Identify these records made from alpaca and llama fibers, most commonly used for keeping track of tribute.
swap.clue: The coarsest wool was instead woven by commoners and used to make chusi, a cloth used for ch'uspa sacks and blankets, or the knotted cords that comprise these recordkeeping devices.

question.text: This Inca city was shaped like a puma and served as the capital of the empire. Legend holds that it was built by Pachacuti.
question.clue: A man who claimed to be a direct descendant of that son two centuries later staged an indigenous uprising before being executed in this city.

swap.text: The Inca used quipu to keep track of the stock of this foodstuff. Along with dried meat known as char'ki, the Inca kept reserves of these freezed-dried potatoes in case of famines.

question.leadin: Part of these people's confederation was ruled by a zipa, who would cover his body in gold dust and jump into Lake Guatavita along with some gold offerings.
question.text: Name these people, whose confederation was ruled by a zipa in the south and a zaque in the north. The last powerful cacique of these people, Tundama, was killed with a large hammer by Balthasar Maldonado.
question.clue: This confederation of Northern Andean tribes that was led by co-rulers called Zipa and Zaque. They were encountered by the Conquistador Gonzalo Jimenez de Quesada after his expedition sailed up the Magdalena.

swap.text: Vilcabamba was founded by this Incan monarch. This monarch was captured by Spanish forces and imprisoned by the brothers of Francisco Pizarro before escaping and laying siege to Cusco for 10 months.

question.leadin: After being attacked by the rival Chanka people, this ruler is said to have called on the sun god Inti to turn stones into pururauca warriors to defend his city.
question.text: Name this son of Viracocha who transformed the Kingdom of Cuzco into the Incan Empire in the 15th century.
question.clue: This king commissioned life-sized gold statues of animals and plant for the central garden of his Coricancha temple.

swap.text: This emperor was responsible for the greatest period of Inca expansion. Though the Inca controlled little more than the valley of Cuzco upon his ascent in 1438, due to a series of successful campaigns his dominion extended from Ecuador to northern Chile and Argentina by the time of his death.
swap.clue: This ruler, who legendarily subjugated the (+) Chanka people with stone warriors, organized his realm into four suyus.

question.leadin: After Pizarro's conquests, this system was initially replaced with the encomienda system typical in the rest of the Spanish Americas.
question.text: Name this Inca system under which all able-bodied men from age 15 to 50 were mandated to work on government projects, often for more than 100 days per year.
question.clue: A revival of this system that ignored traditional boundaries was created by Francisco de Toledo to support the new mining town of Huancavelica.

swap.leadin: Identify some more things about the history of New Spain.
swap.text: This fifth Viceroy of Peru instituted namesake civil reforms after being appointed in 1568. His accomplishments include a less exploitative labor system and the execution of Tupac Amaru.

question.leadin: Richard MacNeish used this term to name an archaeological phase that includes Cob Swamp in Belize.
question.text: Give this name of a period in which earthquake-resistant nettings called shicras were developed. Caral and Kotosh date from a period of the Andean Late Archaic of this name, which indicates the absence of a technology later perfected by the Moche.

swap.leadin: John Rick analyzed the acoustics of the central building in this place, noting that it was designed to encourage a feeling of sounds coming from every direction at once.
swap.text: Identify this archaeological site in Peru, where religious rituals took place as early as 1200 BCE. The only entrance to the Old Temple at this site faced the Mosna River to the east.
swap.clue: This site, which was excavated by Julio C. Tello ("TAY-yo") and is located east of the Cordillera ("cor-di-YEH-ra") Blanca. This site was the centre of a namesake culture which domesticated camelids.
